title: QR Location Helper: Codes That Open Maps
description: Format coordinates or Plus Codes for QR generation with the QR Location Helper — geo URIs and map links any QR app can encode. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the text 'geo:40.7580,-73.9855' is all a QR code needs to open Times Square in a phone's map app — this helper formats that payload correctly, every time.
quick_answer: The QR Location Helper formats latitude/longitude or Plus Codes into the payloads QR codes carry — geo: URIs and map links that open the place when scanned. Enter the location and copy the correctly formatted text into any QR generator: signs, invitations and field markers that phones understand instantly.
steps_intro: A QR code is only as good as its payload. Format it right:

body.t: A printed code at the car park opens the exact viewpoint, gate or bothy in every visitor's phone — the
supplies codes for places with no address to print.
Weddings, site visits, open days: the invitation's QR opens the venue pin, not the postcode's approximate neighbourhood.
Equipment tags and monitoring stations carry codes that open their own locations for the next technician.
The key-box, the gate, the exact door — locations prose describes badly and a scanned map nails instantly.
'geo:40.7580,-73.9855' is the universal payload: Android opens it in maps natively, and as a fallback the helper formats the equivalent https map link that every phone handles.
For address-less places, the payload carries the code ('87G8Q257+6Q New York' style in a maps link) — scannable directions to a place with no street to name.

faq: The maps URL is the safest universal payload; the geo: URI is the cleanest on Android. For a mixed audience, print the URL form.
How precise should the coordinates be?
Five decimals (1.1 m grain) is plenty for a doorway; more decimals make denser QR codes that scan worse in rain and low light.
Longer payloads mean more modules in the square. Short payloads (short links, codes instead of URLs) print bigger modules that survive weather and cheap cameras.
Can I encode a Plus Code instead?
Yes — the helper formats code-based payloads for places whose coordinates would be meaningless to read aloud.
A plain payload tracks nobody. If your generator wraps links in its own shortener, the tracking is the shortener's — read its terms.
Pair the QR with the written address anyway — phones die, grandparents persist. The code is the accelerator, not the only road.
As a rule, the code's width in centimetres should exceed the scanning distance in metres times ten (10 cm code for a metre's reach) — and always test at the real distance.
